claim_boundary: This protocol governs only the prospective closure-audit run. It does not reinterpret or mutate the three historical runs governed by protocol cba33aab... .

commitments.question: Is the material Praxis identity measured from the repository and files actually used?
commitments.prior_understanding: Historical generated evidence included a source-coded Praxis commit value even though validator execution itself was real.
commitments.hypothesis: Praxis HEAD, cleanliness, validator digest, helper digest, and schema digests can be observed read-only and bound to the same validator invocation.
commitments.prediction: The new run will contain machine-readable Praxis identity evidence obtained from Git and file bytes, with no source-coded commit identity.
commitments.alternative_explanation: Executing the correct path alone does not establish repository HEAD or file content identity.
commitments.contradiction_condition: Identity fields are absent, hardcoded, inconsistent with direct remeasurement, or refer to a different validator/schema instance.

commitments.question: Are prediction comparisons causally specific rather than derived from global gate status?
commitments.prior_understanding: The historical comparisons_for(result) assigned one status to every prediction.
commitments.hypothesis: Per-prediction contracts can map only relevant check IDs and evidence to SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED, or INCONCLUSIVE independently.
commitments.prediction: Focused tests will demonstrate mixed outcomes in one comparison set, and the new run record will carry check/evidence traceability for each prediction.
commitments.alternative_explanation: A richer-looking record could still derive every comparison from one global result.
commitments.contradiction_condition: The model accepts global status as an input, unrelated checks affect a prediction, or synthetic mixed outcomes cannot be represented.

commitments.question: Can the run machinery operationally record unexpected evidence?
commitments.prior_understanding: Historical run records always assigned a literal empty list.
commitments.hypothesis: Actual runtime, Praxis, platform, and evidence outcomes can feed a classifier whose empty result means no configured anomaly was observed.
commitments.prediction: Focused tests will inject synthetic anomalies and obtain classified records, while the decisive run will derive—not hardcode—its own list.
commitments.alternative_explanation: A schema field may exist without any production path capable of populating it.
commitments.contradiction_condition: Synthetic anomalies cannot populate the channel or production still assigns an unconditional empty list.

commitments.question: Does machine-generated candidate learning remain evidence-dependent and non-governing?
commitments.prior_understanding: Historical candidate_learning was a fixed prose list emitted independently of individual comparison evidence.
commitments.hypothesis: Candidate proposals can be emitted only when their declared prediction dependencies are supported and can carry explicit non-adoption authority.
commitments.prediction: Tests will show unsupported dependencies suppress a proposal, and emitted proposals will cite comparisons/evidence with governance_adoption set to none.
commitments.alternative_explanation: Renaming a fixed learning list would not repair its epistemic authority.
commitments.contradiction_condition: A proposal appears without supported dependencies/evidence or receives project/Praxis adoption automatically.

commitments.question: Are historical evidence and exact committed protocol bytes reconstructible without rewriting past runs?
commitments.prior_understanding: The historical chain validates, but its protocol was recoverable only from the current mutable protocol path.
commitments.hypothesis: Content-addressed protocol archives plus immutable-prefix verification can preserve bytes and detect changes without editing historical records.
commitments.prediction: Both historical and new protocol digests will recompute from archives, each new run will contain its exact snapshot, and all 93 historical files will retain their pre-audit aggregate digest.
commitments.alternative_explanation: A digest without retained bytes cannot reconstruct content after the current file changes.
commitments.contradiction_condition: An archive digest differs, a run lacks its snapshot, or any historical record/hash/content digest changes.

commitments.question: Can Praxis 0.1 truthfully represent a governed project before its first authorized commit?
commitments.prior_understanding: The schema requires nonempty last-verified provenance, and the unchanged validator requires a referenced gate/evidence plus commit ancestry.
commitments.hypothesis: No truthful SRF representation can satisfy the current generic validator while the project has no verified milestone, no HEAD, and no authority to commit.
commitments.prediction: The actually observed current Praxis validator will fail closed against the honest SRF pre-history state.
commitments.alternative_explanation: Praxis may have changed since the historical observation, so identity and actual output must outrank the expected narrative.
commitments.contradiction_condition: The observed validator passes, crashes, changes relevant identity during the run, or fails for an outcome other than the predicted pre-history boundary.

candidate_learning_contracts.proposal: Material external identities should be observed from the dependency instance actually used, not asserted in project source.
Reflexive run records should preserve independent comparisons, operational anomaly capture, and evidence-dependent non-governing learning proposals.
Digest commitments require recoverable content snapshots when Git history or an external archive is absent.
The Praxis bootstrap representation gap remains a candidate for separate Praxis evaluation under the exact observed Praxis identity.
